cards.explanation: The answer is his sister. Verse 11 says Jehoshabeath, King Jehoram's daughter and the wife of Jehoiada the priest, was Ahaziah's sister. Ahaziah was Joash's father and the king of Judah. So the one who snatched little Joash away was his own father's sister. Family trees get tangled fast, friends.

The answer is in the house of God. Verse 12 says Joash remained hidden with them in the house of God. Jehoiada was a priest, so I think that put him right where Jehoiada worked. Earlier, Jehoshabeath had put him and his nurse in a bedroom (2 Chronicles 22:11). A tiny king tucked away in a bedroom, friends, and the whole thing stayed quiet.

The answer is six. Verse 12 says Joash remained hidden for six years while Athaliah ruled the land. Athaliah was Ahaziah's mother, the one who set out to destroy the royal heirs (2 Chronicles 22:10). Then in the seventh year, Jehoiada makes his move (2 Chronicles 23:1). Six years of waiting, friends, is a LONG time.

The answer is the Levites. Verse 2 says they gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah, along with the heads of the families of Israel. The Levites were the ones who served at the house of God, and Jehoiada was a priest, so they were his kind of crowd. Then they all came to Jerusalem. That's a lot of road trips for one plan, friends.

The answer is that the LORD promised it to David's line. Jehoiada says, “He must reign, just as the LORD promised concerning the descendants of David.” (2 Chronicles 23:3) So the reason is a promise, and the promise came from the LORD. Joash was a descendant of David, and he was the king's son. The whole plan rests on that, friends.

The answer is True. Jehoiada says, “No one is to enter the house of the LORD except the priests and those Levites who serve…” (2 Chronicles 23:6). He adds that they may enter because they are consecrated. Everyone else is to obey the requirement of the LORD. A short guest list, friends, and he means it.

The answer is False. The text says, “…for Jehoiada the priest had not released any of the divisions.” (2 Chronicles 23:8) So each of them took his men, both those coming on duty and those going off. That's a full house, friends.

The answer is David. Verse 9 says Jehoiada gave the commanders the spears and the large and small shields of King David that were in the house of God. David was the one the LORD made the promise about (2 Chronicles 23:3). Those weapons were still there waiting. Somebody kept them better than I kept my edges.

The answer is the crown. Verse 11 says Jehoiada and his sons brought out the king's son and put the crown on him. They also presented him with the Testimony, proclaimed him king and anointed him, and they shouted, “Long live the king!” Hidden for six years, then crowned, friends. Talk about a glow-up.

The answer is that she tears her clothes and screams. Verse 13 says Athaliah tore her clothes and screamed, “Treason, treason!” She walked in and saw the king by his pillar, the trumpeters and the rejoicing crowd. I think she did not get the welcome she was expecting. Quite the entrance, friends.

The answer is False. The text says, “She must not be put to death in the house of the LORD.” (2 Chronicles 23:14) So Jehoiada sends the commanders to bring her out between the ranks. She is seized as she reaches the entrance of the Horse Gate on the palace grounds (2 Chronicles 23:15). This is a heavy part, friends.

The answer is True. Verse 16 says Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and the king and the people that they would be the LORD's people. That means the priest, the king and the people are all in it together. A new king and a new promise, friends.

The answer is that they tear it down. Verse 17 says all the people went to the temple of Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and idols to pieces, too. Baal was a false god, and his temple, altars and idols all came down. That's a lot of smashing, friends.

The answer is the Levitical priests. Verse 18 says Jehoiada put the oversight of the house of the LORD into the hands of the Levitical priests, whom David had appointed over the house of the LORD. Their job was to offer burnt offerings to the LORD as written in the Law of Moses. They were to do it with rejoicing and song, as ordained by David. The right people for the right job, friends.

The answer is False. Verse 19 says Jehoiada stationed gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the LORD, so that no one who was in any way unclean could enter. The gates were watched, not wide open. Even my bakery has a door policy, friends.

The answer is throne. Verse 20 says they seated King Joash on the royal throne. They had brought him down from the house of the LORD and into the palace through the Upper Gate. He was a boy hidden in a bedroom six years before (2 Chronicles 22:12). Now look at him, friends.

The answer is quiet. Verse 21 says all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet, because Athaliah had been put to the sword. Earlier in the passage it was loud with trumpets and cheering (2 Chronicles 23:13). Now things settle down. Quiet after all that noise, friends, I know that feeling after a big batch.
